findings.note: _atomic_write_bytes() recursively creates target.parent and later fsyncs only that directory; it never fsyncs the ancestor containing a newly created parent entry. Thus, on a first Full-track publication where the generated/ parent is absent, a power loss after successful verification and journal removal can preserve the facet manifest and Evidence while losing the generated/ directory entry and Context Projection, leaving a mixed generation without a recoverable journal. _publish_bundle() has the analogous gap when its staging mkdir creates specs/<feature>: it fsyncs the new feature directory and staging ancestors but not specs/, whose entry makes that directory durable. The captured focused tests pre-create the relevant live parents through sentinel setup, so their 395/0 result does not exercise this case. This violates the crash-safe publication guarantee and AC-047; every newly created directory entry must have its containing directory fsynced before the journal can be discarded, or publication must require verified, durably pre-existing target parents.
